item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＮＹ市場サマリー（8日）＝ドル軟調、利回り低下　Ｓ＆Ｐ・ナスダック下落 6:53 配信

＜為替＞ ユーロ圏の国債利回り上昇を受けたユーロ売り・ドル買いの動きが一服する中、ドルが軟調に推移した。一方、年内の米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）の金利見通しに対する予想はおおむね維持された    原油価格の急騰でインフレ懸念が強まる中、ユーロ圏の国債利回りは再び大幅に上昇。フランスやイタリアなど債務水準の高い国の国債に売りが集中した。     シムコープのクリストフ・ション氏は「他の多くの通貨は金融政策見通しと逆相関関係にあるように見えるが、それは全てをドルとＦＲＢが支配していたためであり、この状況はここ数週間続いている」と指摘。その上で「興味深いのは、現在ユーロに影響を及ぼす別の要因、つまりフランスとスペインの政治危機が存在することだ」とし、現在は金利差や金融政策ではなく、ユーロ特有の危機がユーロに影響を及ぼしていると述べた。    一方、ＦＲＢが１０月２７─２８日に開く連邦公開市場委員会（ＦＯＭＣ）での利上げ観測は依然として低い。    ＦＲＢのウォラー理事は８日、インフレ率をＦＲＢの目標である２％まで引き下げるには、追加の利上げが必要になる可能性が高いと述べた。しかし、利上げのペースについては「柔軟性」があり、１０月のＦＯＭＣで利上げをいったん見送る可能性も残した。    ＦＲＢが７日公表した９月のＦＯＭＣ議事要旨によると、利上げの理由を巡って当局者の見解が分かれていた。     主要通貨に対するドル指数は０．０８％安の１０２．１７。一時、１０２．４６まで上昇していた。    ドルは対円で０．１２％安の１５７．８８円。日銀は、原材料コスト上昇による価格引き上げの動きが消費財に波及しており、より頻繁に値上げを実施する企業もあると指摘し、インフレ圧力の拡大に対する懸念を示した。    ユーロは０．０８％高の１．１２０４ドル。一時、１．１１７１ドルまで下落した。     英ポンドは０．０７％高の１．３２１９ドル。

ＮＹ外為市場：[USD/J]

＜債券＞ 国債利回りが概ね低下した。低下は今週で２度目。３０年債入札で堅調な需要が確認されたことを受け、足元の売り局面にもかかわらず、投資家が長期ゾーン国債の買い意欲を維持していることが示された。    取引序盤は原油高が米国債相場の重しとなっていたものの、トランプ米大統領が１１月の米中間選挙前に米国がイランを攻撃することはないと発言したことを受け、原油は小幅に値を戻した。      アナリストは、３０年債入札への堅調な需要がこの日の相場上昇の大きな要因になったと指摘。最高落札利回りは５．６１８％と、入札締め切り時点の予想利回りを下回った。応札倍率は２．５４倍と、過去６回の入札平均である２．４１倍を上回る水準となった。    インフラストラクチャー・キャピタル・マネジメントのジェイ・ハットフィールド最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は、債券市場で１０年債利回りがおそらくピークを付けたと考えているとし、「ピークは恐らく５．３０％近辺、あるいはそれより低い水準だったのではないかと思う」と指摘。米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）による利上げを巡る悲観論もすでにピークを打ったと考えていると述べた。同氏はＦＲＢが今回のサイクルで利上げできるのは１回のみと予想。現在市場が織り込んでいる３回に対して慎重な見方を示した。    １０年債利回りは５ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）低下の５．２２７％。前日には２４年ぶりの高水準を付けていた。    ３０年債利回りは５．９ｂｐ低下の５．６０２％。    金利見通しを反映する２年債利回りは１．３ｂｐ低下の４．７５１％。    ２年債と１０年債の利回り格差は４７．１ｂｐ。序盤には５４．２ｂｐと、８月中旬以来の大きさとなる場面もあった。    ＦＲＢのウォラー理事が８日、インフレ率をＦＲＢの目標である２％まで引き下げるには、追加の利上げが必要になる可能性が高いとしつつ、利上げのペースについては「柔軟性」があると発言したことを受け、２年債利回りは上昇し、上げ幅は１０年債利回りを上回った。

米金融・債券市場：[US/BJ]

＜株式＞ 米国株式市場はＳ＆Ｐ総合５００種・ナスダック総合が下落して取引を終えた。中東情勢の緊迫化と米国の原油生産減少を受けて原油価格が急伸し、インフレや利上げへの懸念が強まった。半導体株の下落も重しとなった。     主要株価指数では、ハイテク株の比重が高いナスダック総合が最も大きな下落率を記録した。同指数は６日に終値で過去最高値を付けていた。    今年に入って８０％超上昇していた半導体株が３．４％安とアンダーパフォームした。オープンＡＩの年換算売上高が、同社が従来示唆していた水準を２００億ドル下回ると英紙フィナンシャル・タイムズ（ＦＴ）が報じたことなどが重しとなった。    ＵＳバンク・ウェルス・マネジメントのチーフ株式ストラテジスト、テリー・サンドベン氏は「市場は来週始まる第３・四半期決算シーズンを前に横ばいで推移している。加えて、イランでの紛争が続き、原油価格を押し上げている」と指摘。「同様に示唆的なのは、年初来、株式相場は上昇しやすい地合いが続いてきたことだ」と述べた。    原油価格は、ホルムズ海峡で船舶への攻撃が相次いだことに加え、ハリケーンの影響による米国の生産減少を巡る懸念から急伸した。    Ｓ＆Ｐ５００種の主要１１業種では、エネルギーが上昇率トップだった。一方、半導体株への売りを背景に情報技術の下落率が最大だった。    メモリー半導体大手の韓国サムスン電子が過去最高の四半期営業益を見込んだものの市場心理の改善にはつながらず、同社株はソウル市場で下落して取引を終えた。競合の米マイクロン・テクノロジーは４．８％下落した。nL6N45T1BN    米紙ウォール・ストリート・ジャーナル（ＷＳＪ）は７日、ブロードコムがオープンＡＩの人工知能（ＡＩ）半導体向けに５００億ドルの資金調達の調整を進めているほか、オラクルも金額は不明だが調達を模索していると報じた。これを受け、ハイテク企業による大規模な債券発行が資本獲得競争を激化させるとの懸念が高まった。    ブロードコムは４．４％、オラクルは５．５％、それぞれ下落した。    飲料大手ペプシコは３．７％高。通期のコア利益見通しを引き下げる一方、追加のコスト削減を進めると表明した。    コーヒーチェーン大手スターバックスは０．４％下落。メキシコ料理チェーンのチポトレ・メキシカン・グリルの買収を模索していると伝わった。チポトレは６．２％急伸した。

米国株式市場：[.NJP]

＜金先物＞ 前日に約２カ月ぶり安値を付けた後、ＦＲＢの利上げ方針や米国債務水準への懸念が交錯する中で小幅に上昇した。金現物は０．４％高の１オンス＝４１２６．７８ドルとなり、米金先物１２月限は０．４％高の４１５７ドルで取引を終えた。

米ドルと米１０年債利回りは２日連続で高水準を維持。ウィズダムツリーのコモディティストラテジスト、ニテシュ・シャー氏は「高水準の債務への懸念が広がる中、金は法定通貨や政府資産の対極として選好されやすい」と指摘した。

ＦＲＢの９月のＦＯＭＣ議事要旨では、利上げの必要性を巡り政策当局者の意見が分かれたことが示された。市場では１０月の利上げ確率が１７％、１２月は８１％と見込まれている。

ＮＹ貴金属：[GOL/XJ]

＜米原油先物＞ 米国時間の原油先物は４％上昇して取引を終えた。中東での紛争継続を巡る懸念が再燃したほか、米南部メキシコ湾岸に接近しているハリケーンによる供給混乱の拡大も意識された。    清算値は、北海ブレント先物が４．０８ドル（４．１％）高の１バレル＝１０４．２８ドル。米ＷＴＩ先物は３．２１ドル（３．６％）上昇の９１．４９ドルとなった。    米国による対イラン攻撃の可能性が懸念されたほか、ハリケーン「イサイアス」が９日に上陸する見通しであることを背景に、両指標とも５ドル超上昇する場面もあった。ブレントは一時、９月２９日以来の高値を付けた。    ただその後、トランプ米大統領が米国がイランと「建設的な」協議を行っているとした上で、１１月の米中間選挙前にイランへの攻撃は実施しないとの考えを表明したことを受け、価格は高値から押し戻された。

ＮＹＭＥＸエネルギー：[CR/USJ]

item.title: US to livestream Army firing squad execution of Fort Hood shooter, Pentagon says
item.description: The US will livestream the Army's upcoming firing squad execution of a gunman who killed 13 people at the Fort Hood military base in 2009, the Pentagon said, in what would be an unprecedented broadcast of a US execution.
item.dc:creator: Phil Stewart
item.content:encoded: The US will livestream the Army's upcoming firing squad execution of a gunman who killed 13 people at the Fort Hood military base in 2009, the Pentagon said, in what would be an unprecedented broadcast of a US execution. Nidal Hasan, a former Army psychiatrist, is set to become the first person to be executed by [USN:L1N45S037 TEXT:"firing squad"] by the US military since 1945. The execution is scheduled for December 3 at the same sprawling Texas base where Hasan opened fire with a laser-sighted handgun in a medical facility. It comes amid heightened debate in the US over the death penalty following the [USN:L1N45M04O TEXT:"botched lethal injection"] of a Tennessee woman last week. "It will be livestreamed. Details will follow," a Pentagon official told Reuters, speaking on the condition of anonymity. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, who championed the push to execute Hasan by firing squad, confirmed plans to livestream the execution in an X post. Media have sought to televise US executions in the past but have been blocked by the courts. No other country is known to televise or livestream a legal execution, experts said. Public executions have become exceedingly rare worldwide. Among countries known to conduct them in recent years are Iran and Taliban-run Afghanistan. Extrajudicial lynchings in the United States, often by white mobs targeting Black Americans, were public spectacles well into the 20th century. The last legally sanctioned public execution in the United States was conducted in 1936, death penalty experts said. Thousands watched that 1936 hanging of a young Black man who had been convicted of raping a white woman. Hegseth told the Human Events Daily program that deciding to execute Hasan by firing squad at Fort Hood on a Thursday at 1 p.m. — the approximate time, day of the week and location of the 2009 shooting — was a "no-brainer." "We'll make sure that people are able to watch it, that it's public. Because people need to understand that ... there's serious consequences for these types of things," Hegseth said. Asked if Hasan had made any final requests, Hegseth said: "Don't care. We'll see him on December 3." PRESIDENT MUST APPROVE FIRING SQUAD EXECUTION A military jury sentenced Hasan to death in August 2013, after finding him guilty of 45 counts of premeditated murder and attempted premeditated murder. The shooting came weeks before Hasan, now 56, was scheduled to be deployed to Afghanistan. He was left partially paralyzed and confined to a wheelchair from being shot by police during his arrest. Under US military law, a US president must approve an execution by firing squad. [USN:L1N45T015 TEXT:"President Donald Trump did so"] on Hegseth's recommendation, the Pentagon said on Monday. The White House declined to say whether Trump supported the livestreaming, referring questions to the Pentagon. The group Death Penalty Action, which opposes capital punishment, said Hasan's execution would be the first military execution since 1961. According to the Death Penalty Information Center, the 1961 execution was carried out by hanging. The last known executions by US military firing squads were in 1945, the center reported. "It would be extremely, extremely strange" to livestream the event, said Eugene Fidell, a lawyer, author and military law expert who lectures at Yale Law School. While firing squads have a long history in American military law, as far as he knew it would be unprecedented to livestream or televise an execution, Fidell said, adding that Hasan would need to sue in federal court if he wanted to block a public display of his death. "The Supreme Court has never addressed this question, and it's an interesting question whether the current Supreme Court would put on their originalist hat and say, 'Well, it was OK in 1790, so what the hell?'" Fidell said. Jonathan Lurie, an author and historian of military justice, said there are no compelling reasons to make the execution public. "What's the point of it? Who would want to see that?" said Lurie. At least five states have firing squads on the books, according to the Death Penalty Information Center. In 2025, [USN:L2N3PP0X8 TEXT:"South Carolina"] carried out the first such execution in the United States in 15 years. Death by firing squad is one of several forms of capital punishment the Trump administration[USN:L6N417125 TEXT:" recently added"] to permissible forms of execution for the gravest of federal crimes, along with electrocution and gas asphyxiation. The number of federal execution options was expanded in part because of increasing difficulties in obtaining drugs for lethal injections, which have also sometimes proved challenging to carry out. Plans by the state of Tennessee to execute a woman for the first time in more than 200 years went awry last week when prison personnel botched attempts to administer a lethal injection, leaving the death-row inmate, Christa Pike, alive but hospitalized. Her lawyers said on Wednesday she awoke "[USN:L1N45T0M9 TEXT:"angry and confused"]" in a hospital. Pike remains very sick and shackled to her hospital bed, they said.

item.title: “ICE is rotten to its core”: NYC Mayor Mamdani slams federal agency after Bronx shooting; claims presence of 5-year-old in car
item.description: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani on Thursday (local time) accused US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) of operating with impunity after a man was shot by federal agents in the Bronx, ...
item.content:encoded:
“ICE is rotten to its core”: NYC Mayor Mamdani slams federal agency after Bronx shooting; claims presence of 5-year-old in car New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani on Thursday (local time) accused US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) of operating with impunity after a man was shot by federal agents in the Bronx, alleging that a five-year-old child was inside the vehicle when the agents opened fire in a crowded residential neighbourhood. ANI | Updated: 09-10-2026 09:43 IST | Created: 09-10-2026 09:43 IST

NYC Mayor Mamdani addressing a press conference on ICE shooting incident (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani on Thursday (local time) accused US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) of operating with impunity after a man was shot by federal agents in the Bronx, alleging that a five-year-old child was inside the vehicle when the agents opened fire in a crowded residential neighbourhood. According to Fox News, while addressing the press, Mamdani said that the shooting took place at around 4 pm (local time) on Thursday in the Marble Hill neighbourhood, adding that several details surrounding the incident remained unclear. He alleged that ICE agents surrounded the man's vehicle before opening fire, at a time when school had just ended, and families and children were on the street. “ICE agents surrounded the man's vehicle before opening fire. They wore construction vests and masks that concealed their faces. There was no reasonable way to identify them as ICE agents. School had just gotten out. The street was crowded with families and children. When ICE agents opened fire, a 5-year-old child, a 5-year-old child, was in the back seat of the car. Thank God that child is physically unharmed,” Mamdani said during the press conference. “We know that ICE is rotten to its core. Today's shooting is only further devastating confirmation of what we have long known, which is that ICE operates with impunity, that they sow chaos and terror across our country, that they have killed far more of our neighbours than they could ever have claimed to save,” he added. Mamdani also said he had spent two hours speaking with US President Donald Trump and Secretary Mullen to negotiate the release of the injured man, but the discussions were unsuccessful. “For the past two hours, I have been on the phone with President Trump and Secretary Mullen negotiating the release of the man ICE agents shot. Those negotiations were unsuccessful. Just moments ago, ICE put the man in an unmarked vehicle and whisked him away. Let me say this plainly: what happened today was an outrage,” Mamdani said, according to Fox News. The US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) said federal agents were attempting to arrest a man from the Dominican Republic when the shooting occurred. According to Fox News, the New York Police Department (NYPD) confirmed that its officers were not present at the scene during the encounter. Earlier on Thursday (local time), the New York City Mayor had called for an end to all ICE enforcement operations in the city. In a post on X, he said early reports indicated that agents had surrounded the man and a five-year-old child inside the car before firing multiple rounds. “This is an unconscionable and incredibly serious situation. I have called the President; when we speak, I will demand that he ends all ICE enforcement actions in our city. I will not stand by while ICE agents terrorize our communities. Our thoughts are with the injured New Yorker and his family tonight. We are praying for his recovery,” Mamdani added in the post. Calling for the agency to leave the city, he said, “Get ICE out of our neighborhoods. Get ICE out of our hospitals. Get ICE off our streets. Get ICE away from our children.” He concluded the post with the words, “Abolish ICE.” Meanwhile, ICE said in a post on X that the incident occurred at approximately 4 pm ET on October 8, when its officers were conducting an operation to arrest a Dominican Republic national with a prior criminal conviction for grand larceny and multiple previous arrests. The agency alleged that the man had associations with the Trinitarios gang. ICE said an officer discharged a weapon during the incident, injuring the individual, and that officers immediately provided medical assistance. “The individual is alive and at a local hospital. The FBI and HSI are on the scene. The incident remains under investigation. More information will be shared as it becomes available,” the agency said. ICE also criticised sanctuary policies, arguing that the release of individuals it considers dangerous makes enforcement operations more unpredictable and puts officers and the public at risk. Following the shooting, anti-ICE protesters gathered outside NewYork-Presbyterian Allen Hospital, where the injured man was being treated, according to the New York Post. The newspaper reported that demonstrators called for ICE to leave the city and that a brief confrontation occurred when some protesters pushed against police barricades. At least one protester was arrested, the report said. A CBS News analysis found that there have been at least 30 shootings involving Department of Homeland Security officers during the second Trump administration, some of which have been fatal. (ANI)

(This story has not been edited by Devdiscourse staff and is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

item.title: OpenAI's September annualized revenue nears $50 billion, less than previously indicated, source says
item.description: OpenAI has told investors its annualized revenue for September was almost $50 billion, a drop from what it signaled earlier, a person familiar with the matter told Reuters on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Jaspreet Singh, Krystal Hu
item.content:encoded: OpenAI has told investors its annualized revenue for September was almost $50 billion, a drop from what it signaled earlier, a person familiar with the matter told Reuters on Thursday. The company previously indicated to investors at a separate event that its revenue run rate for last month was [USN:L4N45L1EC TEXT:"approaching $70 billion"], Reuters and other media reported. The discrepancy mainly arose from an attempt to produce a direct comparison with figures from rival Anthropic, the person said on condition of anonymity. OpenAI did not respond to a request for comment. The latest revenue figure was first reported by the Financial Times. OpenAI, unlike Anthropic, does not include, for instance, revenue from sales via cloud partners such as Amazon's (AMZN.O) AWS and Alphabet's (GOOGL.O) Google Cloud. Anthropic pays cloud partners [USN:L6N45K15A TEXT:"about 16% of every dollar"] earned through them, which last year accounted for half of revenue, a Reuters analysis showed. Both OpenAI and Anthropic are preparing to go public, a process through which Wall Street is likely to gain a clearer view of finances, including the sustainability of rapid revenue growth brought about by a boom in demand for AI applications. OpenAI started this year with $20 billion in annualized revenue versus $6 billion in 2024. Its quarterly revenue was eclipsed by Anthropic for the first time in the second quarter, with OpenAI reporting $6.7 billion compared to Anthropic's $11.5 billion. Anthropic's annualized revenue crossed $65 billion in July, and is set to reach $100 billion by year-end, sources previously told Reuters. Analysts consider annualized revenue run rate a sometimes misleading sales metric, which often involves multiplying one month's revenue by 12. It has nonetheless become a popular metric among fast-growing Silicon Valley startups.

item.title: Aritzia Q2 profit roughly triples to $201.7 million as U.S. revenues grow
item.description: Aritzia Inc.’s second-quarter earnings roughly tripled from last year as the company expanded further outside Canada.
item.dc:creator: The Canadian Press
item.content:encoded: Aritzia Inc.’s second-quarter earnings roughly tripled from last year as the company expanded further outside Canada. The Vancouver-based retailer says its net income for the period ended Aug. 30 increased by 204 per cent from last year to $201.7 million. That amounted to $1.70 per diluted share compared with 56 cents a year before. Over the same period, its net revenue increased 44 per cent to $1.17 billion. Almost $780 million of that revenue was derived in the U.S., where the company has been opening more stores. The strength of the quarter has encouraged Aritzia to boost its guidance. It now expects to close out the year with between $4.78 billion and $4.88 billion, which would be an increase of up to 32 per cent from last year. --- Tara Deschamps, The Canadian Press This report by The Canadian Press was first published Oct. 8, 2026.

Arathy Somasekhar

item.content:encoded:
原油先物4％高、中東緊迫化とメキシコ湾ハリケーン接近で 5:36 配信

ホルムズ海峡を航行する船舶。オマーン・ムサンダムから２日撮影。REUTERS/Stringer

Arathy Somasekhar

[ヒューストン　８日　ロイター] - 米国時間の原油先物は４％上昇して取引を終えた。中東での紛争継続を巡る懸念が再燃したほか、米南部メキシコ湾岸に接近しているハリケーンによる供給混乱の拡大も意識された。

清算値は、北海ブレント先物が４．０８ドル（４．１％）高の１バレル＝１０４．２８ドル。米ＷＴＩ先物は３．２１ドル（３．６％）上昇の９１．４９ドルとなった。

米国による対イラン攻撃の可能性が懸念されたほか、ハリケーン「イサイアス」が９日に上陸する見通しであることを背景に、両指標とも５ドル超上昇する場面もあった。ブレントは一時、９月２９日以来の高値を付けた。

ただその後、トランプ米大統領が米国がイランと「建設的な」協議を行っているとした上で、１１月の米中間選挙前にイランへの攻撃は実施しないとの考えを表明したことを受け、価格は高値から押し戻された。

item.title: Rising oil prices, falling technology stocks and reversing bond yields keep Wall Street unsettled
item.description: Jumping oil prices are sending bond yields higher and stocks lower on Wall Street, as the price for a barrel of Brent climbs back toward US$105.
item.dc:creator: The Associated Press
item.content:encoded: NEW YORK — Some sharp reversals kept financial markets unsteady on Thursday, as oil prices rose and U.S. stock indexes finished mixed. The S&P 500 fell 0.5 per cent for a second straight loss after setting its all-time high. The Dow Jones Industrial Average added 51 points, or 0.1 per cent, and the Nasdaq composite fell 1.3 per cent as technology stocks took particularly hard hits. Stocks felt pressure from a 4.1 per cent rise in the price for a barrel of Brent crude oil, the international standard, to US$104.28. It’s been pinballing between US$96 and nearly US$110 over the last month on uncertainty about when the war with Iran will allow the global energy industry to return to normal. Brent got to nearly US$106 in the morning before President Donald Trump sent its price veering after saying “productive discussions” are happening with Iran and that the U.S. military would not attack it before the upcoming U.S. elections in November. That briefly sent Brent toward US$103 before it eventually turned back upward. Even sharper swings shook the bond market, where yields have been jumping worldwide to their highest levels in years or even decades, which threaten to slow the economy. The 10-year Treasury yield initially rose with oil prices, going from 5.28 per cent late Wednesday to 5.35 per cent early Thursday morning. But it then fell all the way back to 5.23 per cent. It dropped after the U.S. government said that it sold US$22 billion in 30-year Treasury bonds at an auction with a high yield of less than 5.62 per cent. That helped bring the 30-year Treasury yield down to 5.60 per cent from 5.73 per cent in the morning, which is a notable move for the bond market. A day earlier, an auction of 10-year Treasurys also helped bring down yields. Strong demand there showed investors are still willing to buy U.S. government debt, even though their prices have fallen sharply this year because of worries about high inflation, big government debt loads and other factors. “Higher U.S. Treasury yields are starting to create their own demand, buyers are showing up for the right price,” said Tony Miano, global investment strategy analyst at Wells Fargo Investment Institute. On Wall Street, the ease in Treasury yields helped the majority of U.S. stocks rise, including two out of every three in the S&P 500 index. PepsiCo climbed 3.7 per cent after the snack and drink company reported stronger profit and revenue for the latest quarter than analysts expected, thanks in part to strength outside of North America. But drops for several influential technology stocks overshadowed such gains. Nvidia, the chip company that’s ridden the tidal wave of demand created by artificial-intelligence technology, fell 2.9 per cent. Because it’s the largest stock by value on Wall Street, it was the heaviest weight on the S&P 500 even though other stocks had larger losses. That included drops for other AI-related stocks, including Broadcom’s 4.3 per cent fall and Micron Technology’s 4.8 per cent slide. The losses came even though a bellwether for the chip industry, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co., reported growth for September that suggested its revenue for the latest quarter was strong enough to top analysts’ expectations. TSMC’s stock that trades in the United States fell 3 per cent. AI stocks are under heavy pressure to report big growth to justify how high their stock prices have soared in recent years because of the AI frenzy. All told, the S&P 500 fell 36.41 points to 7,765.36. The Dow Jones Industrial Average added 51.77 to 51,231.64, and the Nasdaq composite slid 345.35 to 27,193.34. In South Korea’s stock market, Samsung Electronics dropped 2.4 per cent to help drag the Kospi index down 2.6 per cent. The tech giant said its operating profit for the latest quarter likely soared to 107.4 trillion Korean won (roughly US$80 billion) from 12.17 trillion won a year earlier, but that wasn’t enough to satisfy investors. In other stock markets abroad, indexes fell across much of the rest of Asia and Europe. ___ Stan Choe, The Associated Press AP Business Writers Chan Ho-him and Michelle Chapman contributed to this report.

米国株式市場＝Ｓ＆Ｐ・ナスダック下落、原油急騰で　半導体株が安い 5:11 配信

2026年10月8日、米ニューヨーク証券取引所（NYSE）REUTERS/Jeenah Moon

［ニューヨーク　８日　ロイター］ - 米国株式市場はＳ＆Ｐ総合５００種・ナスダック総合が下落して取引を終えた。中東情勢の緊迫化と米国の原油生産減少を受けて原油価格が急伸し、インフレや利上げへの懸念が強まった。半導体株の下落も重しとなった。

主要株価指数では、ハイテク株の比重が高いナスダック総合が最も大きな下落率を記録した。同指数は６日に終値で過去最高値を付けていた。

今年に入って８０％超上昇していた半導体株が３．４％安とアンダーパフォームした。オープンＡＩの年換算売上高が、同社が従来示唆していた水準を２００億ドル下回ると英紙フィナンシャル・タイムズ（ＦＴ）が報じたことなどが重しとなった。

ＵＳバンク・ウェルス・マネジメントのチーフ株式ストラテジスト、テリー・サンドベン氏は「市場は来週始まる第３・四半期決算シーズンを前に横ばいで推移している。加えて、イランでの紛争が続き、原油価格を押し上げている」と指摘。「同様に示唆的なのは、年初来、株式相場は上昇しやすい地合いが続いてきたことだ」と述べた。

原油価格は、ホルムズ海峡で船舶への攻撃が相次いだことに加え、ハリケーンの影響による米国の生産減少を巡る懸念から急伸した。

Ｓ＆Ｐ５００種の主要１１業種では、エネルギーが上昇率トップだった。一方、半導体株への売りを背景に情報技術の下落率が最大だった。

メモリー半導体大手の韓国サムスン電子が過去最高の四半期営業益を見込んだものの市場心理の改善にはつながらず、同社株はソウル市場で下落して取引を終えた。競合の米マイクロン・テクノロジーは４．８％下落した。

米紙ウォール・ストリート・ジャーナル（ＷＳＪ）は７日、ブロードコムがオープンＡＩの人工知能（ＡＩ）半導体向けに５００億ドルの資金調達の調整を進めているほか、オラクルも金額は不明だが調達を模索していると報じた。これを受け、ハイテク企業による大規模な債券発行が資本獲得競争を激化させるとの懸念が高まった。

ブロードコムは４．４％、オラクルは５．５％、それぞれ下落した。

飲料大手ペプシコは３．７％高。通期のコア利益見通しを引き下げる一方、追加のコスト削減を進めると表明した。

コーヒーチェーン大手スターバックスは０．４％下落。メキシコ料理チェーンのチポトレ・メキシカン・グリルの買収を模索していると伝わった。チポトレは６．２％急伸した。

ニューヨーク証券取引所では値上がり銘柄数が値下がり銘柄数を１．２８対１の比率で上回った。ナスダックでは１．３３対１で値下がり銘柄が多かった。

米取引所の合算出来高は１８８億１０００万株。直近２０営業日の平均は１７７億４０００万株。

Explainer-The skilled foreign tech workers' green card program under attack from Trump

Office workers are seen at a building in downtown San Francisco, in California, U.S., February 23, 2024. REUTERS/Carlos Barria/File Photo

FAST

Oct 8 : The US government said on Thursday it is suspending some of the world's biggest tech and IT firms including Microsoft, Cognizant and Capgemini from a key green card program that allows skilled foreign workers to gain permanent residency through their employment.  Senior US officials cited alleged fraud as the reason behind the move, saying companies have been using the program to replace American workers with cheaper foreign workers, and comes as the latest step in the Trump administration's crackdown on skilled foreign labor.  WHAT IS UNDER SUSPENSION? The suspension is targeting a key employer-sponsorship mechanism, called the Permanent Labor Certification or PERM, which is used by major technology companies and outsourcing firms. The US government said that for certain companies, it would not accept any new PERM applications or process any pending ones.

PERM came into effect in 2005, aiming to speed up the long processing times experienced under the previous paper-based "Alien Employment Certification" program. Under the program, the US Department of Labor (DOL) allows an employer to sponsor a foreign worker permanent residency. The process is initiated by qualified US employers, and not individual workers. The Labor Department must certify to the US Citizenship and Immigration Services that there are not enough US workers that are qualified and available for a given job opportunity, and that the employment of the foreign worker will not affect the wages and working conditions of similarly employed Americans.  Outside of PERM and family-based routes to permanent residency, individuals can also self-petition for green cards through processes such as the EB-1A application for individuals with extraordinary ability or the EB-2 National Interest Waiver. WHY IS IT IMPORTANT?  The PERM program serves as a critical bridge between temporary work status and a green card for many foreign skilled workers. Many IT firms employ hundreds of thousands of workers who typically start on temporary work visas such as the H-1B, and later seek permanent residency.  Without the option to be sponsored by their employer under PERM, foreign workers could lose a key route to permanent residency and would have to stay on temporary visas for longer. For companies, recruiting foreign talent could become harder, as many workers overseas view the path to permanent US residency as a key reason for taking a job.  WHICH COMPANIES ARE UNDER SUSPENSION?  The US said it is suspending Microsoft and Adobe along with some of the largest IT firms in the world, including Cognizant, Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services, Wipro, HCL Technologies and Capgemini.    Other companies such as Meta, Amazon or Alphabet's Google remain free to participate in the program.  WHY IS THE US FREEZING APPLICATIONS? The move widens an ongoing crackdown on visas which the Trump administration has said cost US jobs. Vice President JD Vance said, without citing specific evidence, companies are using the PERM program to replace American employees with foreign workers and undercut their wages.  Vance said on Thursday: "Our message to Microsoft is: You're a great American company, but you've got to hire great American workers." The suspensions follow President Trump's move to impose a one-time $100,000 fee on new H-1B visa petitions for highly skilled foreign workers, which has been blocked by federal court orders.  HOW IS PERM DIFFERENT FROM H-1B? H-1B is a temporary work visa that allows skilled foreign workers to work in the US, generally for up to six years. PERM meanwhile is a permanent labor-certification process. The freeze does not appear to directly affect current holders of H-1B visas.  HOW CURTAILING PERM COULD BACKFIRE Some experts said that while the PERM suspensions might target specific companies, such policies risk making the US less competitive globally by deterring highly skilled foreign talent. "It is a fallacy to think that you can protect American workers by keeping skilled foreign workers out of the country. You think that foreign talent competes with Americans within our borders, they'll certainly compete with Americans by working abroad," said Chad Sparber, Director of the Lampert Institute for Civic and Global Affairs at Colgate University. Ahmet Gulek, Postdoctoral Fellow at Stanford’s Immigration Policy Lab, said that permanent residency is the primary way for talented foreign workers to stay in the country and without it, some will leave, and some will not come in the first place, even temporarily.

Source: Reuters

item.content:encoded:
ＮＹ外為市場＝ドル軟調、欧州国債売り一服　円は157円台後半 4:54 配信

写真は米ドル紙幣。2025年4月、インドネシア・ジャカルタの両替所で撮影。REUTERS/Willy Kurniawan

Chuck Mikolajczak

[ニューヨーク　８日　ロイター] - ニューヨーク外為市場では、ユーロ圏の国債利回り上昇を受けたユーロ売り・ドル買いの動きが一服する中、ドルが軟調に推移した。一方、年内の米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）の金利見通しに対する予想はおおむね維持された

原油価格の急騰でインフレ懸念が強まる中、ユーロ圏の国債利回りは再び大幅に上昇。フランスやイタリアなど債務水準の高い国の国債に売りが集中した。

シムコープのクリストフ・ション氏は「他の多くの通貨は金融政策見通しと逆相関関係にあるように見えるが、それは全てをドルとＦＲＢが支配していたためであり、この状況はここ数週間続いている」と指摘。その上で「興味深いのは、現在ユーロに影響を及ぼす別の要因、つまりフランスとスペインの政治危機が存在することだ」とし、現在は金利差や金融政策ではなく、ユーロ特有の危機がユーロに影響を及ぼしていると述べた。

一方、ＦＲＢが１０月２７─２８日に開く連邦公開市場委員会（ＦＯＭＣ）での利上げ観測は依然として低い。

ＦＲＢのウォラー理事は８日、インフレ率をＦＲＢの目標である２％まで引き下げるには、追加の利上げが必要になる可能性が高いと述べた。しかし、利上げのペースについては「柔軟性」があり、１０月のＦＯＭＣで利上げをいったん見送る可能性も残した。

ＦＲＢが７日公表した９月のＦＯＭＣ議事要旨によると、利上げの理由を巡って当局者の見解が分かれていた。

主要通貨に対するドル指数は０．０８％安の１０２．１７。一時、１０２．４６まで上昇していた。

ドルは対円で０．１２％安の１５７．８８円。日銀は、原材料コスト上昇による価格引き上げの動きが消費財に波及しており、より頻繁に値上げを実施する企業もあると指摘し、インフレ圧力の拡大に対する懸念を示した。

ユーロは０．０８％高の１．１２０４ドル。一時、１．１１７１ドルまで下落した。

英ポンドは０．０７％高の１．３２１９ドル。

FAST

WASHINGTON, Oct 8 : More than 120 US lawmakers raised concerns on Thursday about a deal for Alphabet's Google unit to acquire defunct carrier Spirit Airlines' internal data for $10 million to train artificial intelligence systems. As part of Spirit's closure and asset liquidation, Google won an auction in August for data from spreadsheets and calendars as well as for marketing, productivity and operations. Spirit Airlines halted operations in May. A privacy ombudsman on Monday recommended a US bankruptcy judge approve the deal at an October 14 hearing after excluding passenger personal information from 97 million Spirit customers. The lawmakers led by Senator Elizabeth Warren and Representative Steven Horsford said the sale would include 100 million emails, 500 million Microsoft Teams messages and other employee records.

The lawmakers asked the company to "exclude employee information from the transaction to the greatest extent possible." "Innovation should not come at the expense of workers’ privacy or the confidentiality of information they were required to provide as a condition of employment," said the lawmakers. "The unprecedented scale and sophistication of modern artificial intelligence make it particularly important that privacy protections keep pace with the technology." Google said it did not want to acquire personal information. "We are not looking to buy any personal information from Spirit. The information will either be completely excluded or will be de-identified by an independent third party before Google receives any data. We're already working constructively with the appointed privacy ombudsman," a Google spokesperson said. Union leaders have expressed concern about the sale. Sara Nelson, president of the Association of Flight Attendants-CWA, said, "The outcome of conditions on this proposed sale to Google carries tremendous implications for workers across the economy." Spirit also received a $7.5 million bid from Mercor, an AI data company, for the employee data. The Federal Aviation Administration this week approved the $58.5 million sale of Spirit's slots at New York LaGuardia airport to JetBlue Airways.

Source: Reuters

Perica, a more than 17-year veteran of Apple's M&A and corporate development function, also took oversight of iCloud, Fitness+ and News, among other businesses, in 2023, the memo written by services chief Eddy Cue said. Here are some details: • Perica will now dedicate his efforts entirely to the services leadership team and report to Cue, the memo said

item.title: Canada’s financial system remains resilient, OSFI says
item.description: The Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions says rapid technological advances have intensified risk in the Canadian financial system.
item.dc:creator: The Canadian Press
item.content:encoded: OTTAWA — The Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions says geopolitical uncertainty, economic change and rapid technological advances have intensified risk in the Canadian financial system. The comments come as the federal banking regulator offered its regular update to its annual risk outlook that was published in the spring. The report focuses on how frontier artificial intelligence can amplify cyber, technology, third-party and reputational risks. It notes that as AI capabilities advance, institutions need to strengthen governance, controls and testing. Peter Routledge, the superintendent of financial institutions, says in an era of advancing AI capabilities, resilience is a competitive advantage. He says financial institutions that use AI responsibly while managing cyber, technology, and third-party risks will position themselves to thrive in a complex environment. --- This report by The Canadian Press was first published Oct. 8, 2026.

item.title: The skilled foreign tech workers' green card program under attack from Trump
item.description: Some experts say such policies risk making the US less competitive globally by deterring highly skilled foreign talent.
item.dc:creator: Deborah Sophia, Jaspreet Singh
item.content:encoded: The US government said on Thursday it is [USN:L6N45U111 TEXT:"suspending"] some of the world's biggest tech and IT firms including Microsoft, Cognizant and Capgemini from a key green card program that allows skilled foreign workers to gain permanent residency through their employment. Senior US officials cited alleged fraud as the reason behind the move, saying companies have been using the program to replace American workers with cheaper foreign workers, and comes as the latest step in the Trump administration's crackdown on skilled foreign labor. WHAT IS UNDER SUSPENSION? The suspension is targeting a key employer-sponsorship mechanism, called the Permanent Labor Certification or PERM, which is used by major technology companies and outsourcing firms. The US government said that for certain companies, it would not accept any new PERM applications or process any pending ones. PERM came into effect in 2005, aiming to speed up the long processing times experienced under the previous paper-based "Alien Employment Certification" program. Under the program, the US Department of Labor (DOL) allows an employer to sponsor a foreign worker permanent residency. The process is initiated by qualified US employers, and not individual workers. The Labor Department must certify to the US Citizenship and Immigration Services that there are not enough US workers that are qualified and available for a given job opportunity, and that the employment of the foreign worker will not affect the wages and working conditions of similarly employed Americans. Outside of PERM and family-based routes to permanent residency, individuals can also self-petition for green cards through processes such as the EB-1A application for individuals with extraordinary ability or the EB-2 National Interest Waiver. WHY IS IT IMPORTANT? The PERM program serves as a critical bridge between temporary work status and a green card for many foreign skilled workers. Many IT firms employ hundreds of thousands of workers who typically start on temporary work visas such as the H-1B, and later seek permanent residency. Without the option to be sponsored by their employer under PERM, foreign workers could lose a key route to permanent residency and would have to stay on temporary visas for longer. For companies, recruiting foreign talent could become harder, as many workers overseas view the path to permanent US residency as a key reason for taking a job. WHICH COMPANIES ARE UNDER SUSPENSION? The US said it is suspending Microsoft (MSFT.O) and Adobe (ADBE.O) along with some of the largest IT firms in the world, including Cognizant (CTSH.O) , Infosys (INFY.NS) , Tata Consultancy Services (TCS.NS) , Wipro (WIPR.NS) , HCL Technologies (HCLT.NS) and Capgemini (CAPP.PA) . Other companies such as Meta (META.O) , Amazon (AMZN.O) or Alphabet's Google (GOOGL.O) remain free to participate in the program. WHY IS THE US FREEZING APPLICATIONS? The move widens an ongoing crackdown on visas which the Trump administration has said cost US jobs. Vice President JD Vance said, without citing specific evidence, companies are using the PERM program to replace American employees with foreign workers and undercut their wages. Vance said on Thursday: "Our message to Microsoft is: You're a great American company, but you've got to hire great American workers." The suspensions follow President Trump's move to impose a one-time $100,000 fee on new H-1B visa petitions for highly skilled foreign workers, which has been blocked by federal court orders. HOW IS PERM DIFFERENT FROM H-1B? H-1B is a temporary work visa that allows skilled foreign workers to work in the US, generally for up to six years. PERM meanwhile is a permanent labor-certification process. The freeze does not appear to directly affect current holders of H-1B visas. HOW CURTAILING PERM COULD BACKFIRE Some experts said that while the PERM suspensions might target specific companies, such policies risk making the US less competitive globally by deterring highly skilled foreign talent. "It is a fallacy to think that you can protect American workers by keeping skilled foreign workers out of the country. You think that foreign talent competes with Americans within our borders, they'll certainly compete with Americans by working abroad," said Chad Sparber, Director of the Lampert Institute for Civic and Global Affairs at Colgate University. Ahmet Gulek, Postdoctoral Fellow at Stanford’s Immigration Policy Lab, said that permanent residency is the primary way for talented foreign workers to stay in the country and without it, some will leave, and some will not come in the first place, even temporarily.

item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
欧州市場サマリー（8日） 3:52 配信

＜ロンドン株式市場＞

続落して取引を終えた。中型株で構成するＦＴＳＥ２５０種指数は０．３９％安だった。原油価格急騰によるインフレ懸念と長期金利の上昇が相場の重荷となった。

英１０年債利回りは一時５．５２７％と１９年ぶりの高水準を付けた。２０年債、３０年債の利回りはいずれも６％を超えた。

ＦＴＳＥ３５０種石油・ガス株指数は３．７４％高。石油大手のＢＰは４．１％、シェルは３．６％それぞれ上昇した。

一方、銀行株指数は１．８０％安。金融大手ＨＳＢＣは１．９％、スタンダード・チャータードは２．０％、ロイズは１．７％、それぞれ値下がりした。

製薬・バイオテクノロジー株指数は２．２４％安。

スーパーマーケット大手のテスコは５．２％高。通期利益見通しを上方修正し、買われた。

ロンドン株式市場：[.LJP]

＜欧州株式市場＞

続落して取引を終えた。ＳＴＯＸＸ欧州６００種指数は約４カ月ぶりの安値を付けた。原油高によるインフレ懸念や長期金利上昇が相場の重荷となり、銀行株など大半の業種の株価が下落した。財政懸念が強いフランスのＣＡＣ４０指数は０．５１％安と、約半年ぶりの安値を付けた。

ＳＴＯＸＸ欧州６００種銀行株指数は２．０４％安。ドイツ銀行は０．７％、フランスのソシエテ・ジェネラルは２．３％、スペインのサンタンデールは２．９％、イタリアのウニクレディトは３．１％、いずれも下落した。

ヘルスケア株指数は２．４７％安。欧州のバイオ医薬品会社アルジェニクスは１５．９％下落した。シェーグレン病の臨床試験で主要目標を達成する見込みが薄いとして試験を中止したことを受け、売られた。

原油先物価格の値上がりを受けて、石油・ガス株指数は２．４２％上昇した。

欧州株式市場：[.FJ]

＜ユーロ圏債券＞

原油価格の急騰を受けてインフレ懸念が強まる中、域内国債利回りが上昇した。ただ、フランスやイタリアなど債務残高が大きい国の国債売りをいったん手控える動きが見られた。

８日の北海ブレント先物は一時、５％高の１バレル＝１０５ドルと、１週間ぶりの高値を付けた。米・イラン戦争や、イエメンの親イラン武装組織フーシ派とサウジアラビアとの紛争を背景に、中東からの原油供給途絶が懸念されている。

エネルギー価格の上昇を受け、市場では欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）による追加利上げ観測が強まった。

ユーロ圏の指標となるドイツ１０年債利回りは２ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）上昇の３．５０％。

ＥＣＢの政策金利見通しに敏感な独２年債利回りは５ｂｐ上昇の３．０８％。

フランス１０年債利回りは２ｂｐ上昇の４．８８％。取引序盤には９ｂｐ上昇する場面もあった。

独仏１０年債利回り格差は１３８ｂｐと２ｂｐ拡大した。

イタリア１０年債利回りは１ｂｐ低下の４．６３％となった。

item.title: ＦＲＢ、物価目標達成に追加利上げ必要＝セントルイス連銀総裁
item.description:
Michael S. Derby
[ニューヨーク ８日 ロイター] - 米セントルイス地区連銀のムサレム総裁は８日、連...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＦＲＢ、物価目標達成に追加利上げ必要＝セントルイス連銀総裁 3:31 配信

２０２５年２月撮影　REUTERS/Brendan McDermid

Michael S. Derby

[ニューヨーク　８日　ロイター] - 米セントルイス地区連銀のムサレム総裁は８日、連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）はインフレ率を目標の２％に戻すために追加利上げを実施する必要があると述べた。ただ、今月下旬の連邦公開市場委員会（ＦＯＭＣ）での対応については言及を避けた。

ムサレム氏はニューヨークで開かれたブルームバーグ主催のイベントで「インフレ率を適時に目標へ戻すには一段の金融引き締めが必要になる」とし、「『適時』を１８カ月程度と考える場合、向こう６─９カ月の適切な時期に追加利上げが必要になることを示唆している」と語った。

ＦＲＢは２７─２８日のＦＯＭＣで利上げを決定すべきかとの質問に対しては「毎回の会合に極めてオープンな姿勢で臨んでおり、その会合の結果や自分がどう行動するかについて予断を持っていない」と述べるにとどめた。ただ、「インフレ動向を踏まえると、追加的な政策引き締めを検討する必要がある」と述べた。ムサレム氏は今年のＦＯＭＣで投票権を持っていない。

このほか、力強い経済成長と安定した労働市場が続く中で、インフレが米経済にとって最大の課題になっていると指摘。雇用を大きく損なうことなくインフレ率を引き下げられる可能性が高く、ＦＲＢが目標とする２％に戻すことで経済全体に幅広く恩恵をもたらすことができるとの見方を示した。

このところ上昇している国債利回りについては、ＦＲＢに対する信認が失われていることを示すものではなく、経済が堅調で資本需要が強い環境下では実質金利が上昇するとの見方が背景にあると指摘。ハイテク部門の旺盛な投資や政府の巨額な資金調達需要も利回りを押し上げる要因になっていると述べた。同時に「米政府は過去２０年近くにわたり持続不可能な財政運営の軌道をたどっている」とし、多額の政府債務が経済に問題を引き起こすリスクが存在すると警告した。

FAST

WASHINGTON, Oct 8 : The four leaders of US President Donald Trump's AI task force are slated to meet on Thursday, task force vice chair Scott Kupor told Reuters, adding that he expects the full committee to convene next week as pressure builds on Washington to take action on AI. The task force is expected to help shape the administration's approach to AI at a pivotal moment for the technology.  Public uneasiness with AI, and the small group of people who seemingly hold sway over it, has risen in recent months. Most US voters think Trump's administration and Congress are not taking the risks of AI seriously enough and want the government to write new regulations for the technology, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll published on Wednesday.  The AI companies "need to step up and demonstrate that they are taking concerns that people have around security and vulnerabilities very seriously, as do we," Kupor said.

Kupor said he expects the group to release a charter outlining its goals and responsibilities after its first full committee meeting. The group will have four to five staff members who will be assigned to the committee full-time, he said. Trump has dubbed the group the Super Intelligence Task Force, using his preferred term for artificial intelligence. It is led by Intelligence Director Jay Clayton, with Kupor, Federal Trade Commission Chair Andrew Ferguson and Defense Department technology lead Emil Michael. Trump calls the Defense Department the Department of War. Kupor said he will focus on engaging industries outside the technology sector, including banking, healthcare and utilities, to better understand how AI could affect their exposure to cyber threats. Michael will work directly with AI developers, Kupor said.

Source: Reuters

item.title: Trump says US will not attack Iran before midterm elections in November
item.description: President Donald Trump said on Thursday that the US will not launch an attack on Iran before November's US midterm congressional elections, asserting that the two countries are having "productive" talks about ending the six-month-old war.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump said on Thursday that the US will not launch an attack on Iran before November's US midterm congressional elections , asserting that the two countries are having "productive" talks about ending the six-month-old war. "We are having productive discussions with the Islamic Republic of Iran," Trump wrote in a post on Truth Social. "We will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the midterm elections to be held in the United States on November 3rd." The war, which began in February when the US and Israel launched strikes on Iran, has helped drive Trump's domestic approval ratings downward and is weighing heavily on his fellow Republicans as they seek to preserve their narrow legislative majorities in November's election. Some 60% of Americans — including one in four Republicans — disapprove of how Trump is handling the situation in Iran, according to a recent Reuters/Ipsos poll. The conflict has pushed gasoline prices sharply higher at a time when voters say their top concern is the cost of living. Trump has repeatedly said he expects oil prices to drop after the elections, but he has not offered a detailed plan for exiting the war. Iran and the US have exchanged proposals in recent weeks aimed at ending the war and reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a vital global energy shipping route. Trump rejected Tehran's latest offer. Iran's state media reported on Thursday that Tehran would not abandon uranium enrichment or hand over its uranium stockpile, citing the head of the country's Atomic Energy Organization, days after US Vice President JD Vance told Reuters that Iran must make "[USN:L1N45T0DK TEXT:"meaningful" reductions"] in its enrichment capacity. The US, Israel and Western allies have long accused Iran of seeking nuclear weapons, an accusation Iran has denied.

item.title: WTO raises merchandise trade growth forecast to 3.9% as AI boom offsets hit from Middle East
item.description: The World Trade Organization is sharply increasing its forecast for merchandise trade growth worldwide this year, more than doubling its earlier prediction.
item.dc:creator: The Associated Press
item.content:encoded: GENEVA — The World Trade Organization is sharply increasing its forecast for merchandise trade growth worldwide this year, more than doubling its earlier prediction to 3.9 per cent as booming AI investments offset a hit from the war in the Middle East. The Geneva-based trade body says global trade chugged along at a hearty pace, as supply chains adapted and AI-related spending poured in to provide “a powerful boost to goods trade.” The revised forecast marks a big jump from an initial WTO forecast in this spring for 1.9 per cent growth for merchandise trade. The figure excludes services trade. The trade body forecast growth next year of 4.1 per cent, up from 2.9 per cent predicted in March. “The revision reflects evidence that global supply chains adapted to disruptions in energy and fertilizer markets, while strong investment in AI-related infrastructure boosted trade in AI-enabling goods,” WTO said. Trade of oil and gas and fertilizer through the Persian Gulf was shaken after the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran began in February. WTO said merchandise trade grew 3.5 per cent in the first half of the year, powered by the artificial intelligence market. “Demand for AI-enabling goods such as semiconductors and servers accounted for 47 per cent of global merchandise trade growth in the first half of 2026, and trade in these products rose by 67 per cent year-on-year, accelerating from the already rapid expansion seen in 2024 and 2025,” WTO said. Robert Steiger, its chief economist, said WTO teams — like most forecasters — have been “surprised” at the strength of the AI investment boom. They anticipated that strong growth in AI-enabling goods like electronics and computers would moderate over time because of already-high growth last year and “market saturation” eventually. “This actually has not happened. Trade in AI-enabling goods grew 16 per cent in value terms in 2024. It grew 31 per cent in value terms in 2025, and it grew an astonishing 67 per cent in the first half of 2026,” he told reporters at WTO headquarters. Liquefied natural gas exports from the Middle East fell by 47 per cent in the first half of the year, while crude oil exports dropped by nearly a quarter, WTO said. But shipments from other suppliers helped limit the decline to roughly 1 per cent for LNG and about 6 per cent for crude. WTO said it expects global GDP to grow 2.6 per cent this year and 2.9 per cent in 2027, even though it predicted that the Middle East conflict will continue to weigh on trade through higher energy prices and transport route disruptions. --- Jamey Keaten, The Associated Press

item.title: Shell partially restarts Pearl gas-to-liquids plant in Qatar
item.description: Shell said on Thursday it had partially restarted its Pearl gas-to-liquids plant in Qatar, as traders said QatarEnergy returned Pearl-GTL naphtha cargoes to the spot market six months after the facility was damaged during the Iran war.
item.dc:creator: Mohi Narayan, Stephanie Kelly, Shadia Nasralla
item.content:encoded: Shell (SHEL.L) said on Thursday it had partially restarted its Pearl gas-to-liquids plant in Qatar, as traders said QatarEnergy returned Pearl-GTL naphtha cargoes to the spot market six months after the facility was damaged during the Iran war. Shell said the move would allow it to build a limited amount of product inventory in storage, while its ability to ship product remains subject to the regional security situation. QatarEnergy has begun offering cargoes that include Pearl-GTL naphtha and resumed some contractual deliveries, signalling some return of products from the facility to a supply-starved market. The war disrupted refinery operations and temporarily shut the Strait of Hormuz, through which about 20% of global oil and liquefied natural gas supplies previously passed. Several traders who participate in the market said QatarEnergy issued a spot tender offering up to 50,000 metric tons of naphtha f four grades including Pearl GTL on a free-on-board basis from Ras Laffan port inside the Strait of Hormuz. The state-owned refiner's last naphtha tender, which also included Pearl GTL grade, was awarded at a discount of $150 to Middle East quotes on FOB basis. It [USN:L4N45R0QO TEXT:"has resumed"] sending contract volumes of naphtha to some buyers. India's Haldia Petrochemicals received its 50,000 metric tons for this quarter, a company executive said on Monday. Shell did not comment on the market tender and QatarEnergy did not respond to a request for comment. Oil companies typically do not comment on tenders. REPAIRS TO TRAIN 2 EXPECTED IN Q1 2027 Shell's wholly owned Pearl, which is fed from Qatar's North gas field, was [USN:L6N4070VH TEXT:"hit"] in March, damaging one of its two processing plants, also known as trains. At full capacity, Pearl can produce 140,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day. Pearl's output also feeds into Shell's downstream supply chain, including its lubricants business. Repairs to the facility's Train 2 are expected to be completed in the first quarter of next year, a Shell spokesperson said. Shell estimated in March that it would take one year to fully repair Pearl. Shell said its ability to sustain safe and reliable operations at Pearl depends on regional security, including the safe passage of shipments through the Strait of Hormuz. The first LNG train under QatarEnergy's North Field East expansion project [USN:L1N45T0GE TEXT:"will be ready"] to start operation in November, two people aware of its plans said, offering Qatar a path to restoring some lost output.

item.title: Trump administration freezes green cards for Microsoft, IT firms, probes universities
item.description: The US suspended Microsoft , major IT outsourcers and software maker Adobe from a key green-card program on Thursday while opening probes into nine top universities, widening a crackdown it says targets fraud and protects American jobs.
item.dc:creator: Akash Sriram, Steve Holland
item.content:encoded: The US suspended Microsoft (MSFT.O) , major IT outsourcers and software maker Adobe (ADBE.O) from a key green-card program on Thursday while opening probes into nine top universities, widening a crackdown it says targets fraud and protects American jobs. Since taking office, US President Donald Trump has pursued a broad effort to reduce the number of foreign-born people in the US and curtail their pathway to residence and citizenship. Thursday's twin actions mark the broadest strike yet against skilled-worker immigration programs — potentially cutting off a common path to permanent residency for foreign tech workers — while putting some of the country's top research universities on notice. "There has been no company in the United States, unfortunately, that has abused the system more than Microsoft," Vice President JD Vance said. He said the company laid off 6,000 American workers last year while benefiting from 6,300 H-1B temporary worker visas and nearly 3,000 green cards. His comments came hours before Trump honored tech billionaires for their contributions to America, including Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella. Nadella once held an H-1B visa, as did Elon Musk, who was also honored, while three of the other CEOs honored are immigrants. Nadella thanked Trump for the medal, saying in a post on X he would continue to advance technology and drive American prosperity. Microsoft is the largest filer of PERM applications, or the [USN:L4N45U1DA TEXT:"permanent labor certification"] process, according to data from the US labor department. Under PERM, which most employment-based green cards require, employers must show a foreign hire will not hurt US workers' wages or jobs. The company said in a statement that about 80% of the H-1B applications it filed in the last fiscal year were to extend or change the status of current employees, not to hire new workers. In July, the company said it would [USN:L4N4380XC TEXT:"cut 4,800 jobs"], or about 2.1% of its global workforce. CRACKDOWN WIDENS Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling said the suspension would also cover Cognizant (CTSH.O) , Infosys (INFY.NS) , Tata Consultancy Services (TCS.NS) , Wipro (WIPR.NS) , HCL Technologies (HCLT.NS) and Capgemini (CAPP.PA) . "We will not accept any new or process any pending permanent labor certification applications involving these companies," Sonderling said. He said these companies had since 2009 sought almost three million foreign workers, and had received over 230,000 H-1B visa approvals and over 100,000 permanent labor certifications. Amazon.com was the largest employer of approved H-1B beneficiaries in fiscal 2026, followed by Tata Consultancy Services, Infosys, Apple and Microsoft, according to US immigration data. Vance said the suspensions would last "as long as it needs to," and that the administration wanted the companies to change how they hire. He said some companies post ineffective job ads, then point to the lack of applicants to justify hiring lower-paid foreign workers. Microsoft said in its statement that it pays its H-1B employees the same as any other employees doing comparable work. Adobe, Cognizant, Infosys, HCL Technologies, Wipro and Capgemini did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Tata Consultancy Services declined to comment. Nasscom, India's IT industry body, said Indian tech companies in the US had significantly reduced their reliance on H-1B visas, and relatively few of their workers sought green cards through the PERM process. In September last year, the Labor Department launched an enforcement drive called "Project Firewall" as a White House proclamation imposed a one-time $100,000 fee on new H-1B petitions for workers hired from abroad. UNIVERSITIES UNDER SCRUTINY Vance also said nine universities, including Harvard, Yale and Stanford, would be investigated for what the administration called the misuse of exchange-visitor visas to undercut American wages. The nine schools also include Brown and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. Labor Inspector General Anthony D'Esposito said subpoenas had already been served. D'Esposito said investigators would examine whether foreign influence, improper financial relationships or visa abuse were compromising federally funded research. “It could have an enormous economic impact on the whole US economy,” said Sarah Spreitzer, a vice president at the American Council on Education, which represents college and university presidents. International students historically spent $40 billion a year while in the US, she said. The probe deepens the administration's [USN:L1N45M14M TEXT:"long-running fight"] with Harvard over foreign students. Last year, the Department of Homeland Security subpoenaed the university over alleged misconduct by international students and its compliance with immigration law. Harvard called that subpoena "unfounded retribution" but said it would comply as far as the law requires. Rapidly changing visa policies caused a sharp drop in international applications to Columbia University and contributed to the university pausing admissions to one of its journalism programs, Reuters reported last week.

item.title: Trump dismisses reports of potential strikes on Iran, says “productive discussions” ongoing, no attacks before midterms
item.description: In a post on Truth Social, Trump said that the blockade on Iranian maritime traffic in the Strait of Hormuz would remain in place while claiming that oil was continuing to flow in record volumes ...
item.content:encoded:
Trump dismisses reports of potential strikes on Iran, says “productive discussions” ongoing, no attacks before midterms In a post on Truth Social, Trump said that the blockade on Iranian maritime traffic in the Strait of Hormuz would remain in place while claiming that oil was continuing to flow in record volumes through the strategic waterways with no Iranian oil involved.  ANI | Updated: 08-10-2026 22:25 IST | Created: 08-10-2026 22:25 IST

US President Donald Trump (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

US President Donald Trump on Thursday dismissed reports of possible fresh strikes against Iran, saying “productive discussions” are underway with Tehran and making clear that the United States will not attack Iran before the November 3 midterm elections. In a post on Truth Social, Trump said that the blockade on Iranian maritime traffic in the Strait of Hormuz would remain in place while claiming that oil was continuing to flow in record volumes through the strategic waterways with no Iranian oil involved. He also reiterated that Iran would not be allowed to possess a nuclear weapon. “We are having productive discussions with the Islamic Republic of Iran. I want to make it clear to everybody that, while Iran is in very bad condition, both Economically and Militarily, and while the Blockade will remain in full force and effect, with Oil flowing in Record Numbers of Barrels through the Hormuz Strait (22 Million Barrels, last night alone, with not one barrel coming from, or going to, Iran!), we will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the Midterm Elections to be held in the United States on November 3rd. IRAN WILL NOT HAVE A NUCLEAR WEAPON!” the post read. Trump's statement came a day after reports that the Pentagon had been instructed to prepare for a possible resumption of major combat operations against Iran, potentially ahead of the midterms. Axios report that Trump had not made a final decision on resuming major combat operations against Iran, but that the Pentagon had been instructed to prepare for possible fresh strikes. According to Axios, citing US officials, the Pentagon instructed US Central Command several days ago to conclude preparations for resuming major combat operations in Iran. The directive did not set a specific date for any potential strikes. US and Israeli officials cited by the publication said renewed combat operations could take place before the US midterm elections, scheduled for November 3, and possibly ahead of Israeli elections expected a week earlier. However, Trump's latest statement ruled out an attack before the US midterm elections while saying that discussions with Iran were continuing. Meanwhile, earlier in the day, Iranian Foreign Minister Seyyed Abbas Araghchi said that Tehran would respond to a US peace proposal within the next few days, noting that the negotiations between Tehran and Washington remained ongoing and that messages were continuing to be exchanged through mediators. “The negotiation process is still ongoing and messages are being exchanged through mediators,” Araghchi said, as quoted by Iranian state media Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting (IRIB). The Iranian Foreign Minister said Tehran had already presented its proposal, referred to as the “Seven-Day Plan”, and had received the US side's views on it. “We presented our plan, which we had presented under the title 'Seven-Day Plan', and we also heard the American side's views on it,” Araghchi said. “We are currently reviewing the views of the Americans and I think we will provide our response within the next few days,” he added. The ongoing diplomatic exchanges are linked to Tehran's proposal for reopening the Strait of Hormuz under a seven-day plan, which Araghchi presented last month during the 81st United Nations General Assembly. Araghchi had said the timeline for the proposal would begin once the United States accepted it. According to Al Jazeera, he said Washington would need to take certain actions under the plan, which could be completed within four to five days. “If they accept this plan tomorrow, the seven days will start from tomorrow,” Araghchi said. He said the required steps were already part of a memorandum of understanding and would not be difficult to implement. Under the proposal, if the US fulfilled the conditions, the Strait of Hormuz could be reopened on the sixth day, followed by renewed talks between Tehran and Washington on the seventh day. Trump had earlier rejected the proposed arrangement, according to The Wall Street Journal. (ANI)

(This story has not been edited by Devdiscourse staff and is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

item.title: Plane damaged at Riyadh airport as Houthis escalate attacks, sources say
item.description: Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis escalated their campaign of strikes against Saudi Arabia on Thursday, trying to shut down the kingdom's airspace and oil facilities with missile fire that has killed three people this week and left a plane badly damaged.
item.dc:creator: Timour Azhari, Federico Maccioni
item.content:encoded: Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis escalated their campaign of strikes against Saudi Arabia on Thursday, trying to shut down the kingdom's airspace and oil facilities with missile fire that has killed three people this week and left a plane badly damaged. The group said it had struck Riyadh airport and warned workers to stay away from energy plants, which would be targeted. Shrapnel from an interception or another projectile hit had left the commercial plane belonging to Saudi state carrier Saudia Airlines heavily damaged after catching fire while parked at an airport terminal on Thursday, three people briefed on the matter said. They said no passengers were believed to have been on the plane at the time but they could not rule out any injuries as a result of the incident. A thick black column of smoke and flames were shown rising from Riyadh airport in video verified by Reuters. Saudi Arabia's government media office, its civil aviation authority and Saudia Airlines did not respond to emailed requests for comment. Lufthansa and Air India said they were [USN:L6N45U10R TEXT:"suspending "]flights to Riyadh after Houthi attacks. Separately, Saudi officials said debris from an intercepted missile had hit a kindergarten and medical complex in Riyadh. The Houthis say they are targeting the kingdom over its support for government forces in Yemen's reignited civil war. Saudi Arabia says it is backing an offensive by Yemen's UN-recognised government to take back territory from the Houthis. The conflict, now an overspill of the US-Iran war , has added new chaos to a region already aflame, and threatens to draw other states into gruelling mountain fighting, with Syria now considering [USN:L1N45U05X TEXT:"deploying troops"] to assist Saudi Arabia. The kingdom has pushed for support from allied nations, including [USN:L6N45T0IX TEXT:"Turkey"] and Pakistan, even if only in a logistical or defensive capacity, as it tries to reverse Houthi gains in southwest Yemen, by the southern entrance to the Red Sea. Those requests have taken on more urgency since Saudi authorities said on Wednesday that three people had been [USN:L1N45T00S TEXT:"killed"] this week in strikes on Riyadh airport and Abha airport in the southwest. DELAYS AND CANCELLATIONS The Houthis have made Saudi airports a focus of their strikes, and the Saudi-led coalition fighting in Yemen said it had destroyed two ballistic missiles launched by the group towards Riyadh and another towards Khamis Mushayt, home to a major airbase. According to data compiled by aviation analytics company Cirium, almost half of departures from Riyadh airport had been cancelled by 1500 GMT, with 31 more cancellations expected for Friday in all Saudi airports. Flight tracker FlightRadar24 indicated numerous delayed arrivals and departures at Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport on Thursday. The airport advised travellers to contact airlines to check the status of flights before trying to travel. Riyadh is due to host a major meeting of energy policy makers, the WPC Energy Congress, this week. Several multinational firms based in Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District (KAFD) told staff to work from home after loud booms were heard on Thursday morning, five people familiar with the matter said, including some affected staff. The Saudi government did not respond to a request for comment, and KAFD was not immediately available for comment. Some diplomats said they had received warnings, and some schools in Riyadh told parents there were orders to shelter in place, though authorities did not issue a public alert. Reuters could not identify the source of the booms. CIVIL WAR REIGNITED BY CONFLICT IN IRAN Yemen's long-running civil war, which paused with a ceasefire in 2022, has erupted again in recent weeks with the Houthis seizing stretches of the Red Sea coast last month, including along the vital Bab el-Mandeb Strait. Their threats to shipping and attacks on Saudi cities and infrastructure have drawn the kingdom back in. This week, Saudi-backed forces launched a [USN:L8N45M1W0 TEXT:"counterattack"], taking back some areas around the strait. However, in a war with several front lines, the Houthis have made gains of their own, surrounding Yemen's third-largest city, Taiz, by taking territory along its main mountain road to Aden. The fighting, which pits the Houthis against a coalition of [USN:L6N45S0PX TEXT:"Saudi-backed forces"] under the internationally recognised government, has led to a humanitarian crisis in the poorest Arab state, displacing 200,000 people since the conflict resumed. One US and one Syrian defence official said Syria was carefully considering options for military support, including defensive aid to protect Saudi Arabia from attacks, or an offensive deployment to help take the fight to the Houthis. In response to a request for comment to the Syrian foreign ministry, a diplomat said Syria stood firmly with Saudi Arabia but that its focus was on domestic priorities such as recovery from its own civil war. NATO-member Turkey said on Wednesday it was sending mainly defensive and technical support to the kingdom to help in the fight against the Houthis. A Turkish official said this was expected to take the form of military equipment, intelligence sharing and weapons systems.

item.title: US suspends Permanent labour certification program for Infosys, Wipro, Tata, Microsoft and others, cites abuse of H1B program
item.description: US Vice President JD Vance on Thursday announced the suspension of Microsoft from the Permanent Labor Certification program, alleging that the company had laid off American workers while benefiting ...
item.content:encoded:
US suspends Permanent labour certification program for Infosys, Wipro, Tata, Microsoft and others, cites abuse of H1B program US Vice President JD Vance on Thursday announced the suspension of Microsoft from the Permanent Labor Certification program, alleging that the company had laid off American workers while benefiting from thousands of H-1B visas and green cards. ANI | Updated: 08-10-2026 21:29 IST | Created: 08-10-2026 21:29 IST

US VP JD Vance with Labour secretary Keith Sonderling and AG Todd Blanche on his left (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

In a far reaching move US Labour Secretary Keith Sonderling has announced that the US Government is suspending from the Permanent Labor Certification Program some of the largest IT outsourcing firms in the world which include Cognizant, Infosys, Tata, Wipro, HCL, and Capgemini . The US Labour department attributed the suspension to multiple active federal investigations even as it also suspended US tech majors Microsoft and Adobe from the program. Speaking at a press conference on fighting visa fraud, US Vice President targeted the tech giants for alleged abuse of the H1B program "The H1-B visa program is meant to allow companies to bring in really the best of the best from outside the United States of America for positions that are completely impossible to fill with American workers. Unfortunately, the program has become rife with fraud," he said Attorney General Todd Blanche said, "This announcement today should send and does send a strong signal to every single employer in the United States that the Trump Administration will not tolerate discrimination against American workers." Vance further targeted tech giant Microsoft, alleging that the company had laid off American workers while benefiting from thousands of H-1B visas and green cards. Vance said Microsoft had laid off 6,000 American workers last year while benefiting from 6,300 H-1B visas and nearly 3,000 green cards. "Microsoft laid off last year, 6000 American workers at the same time the company benefited from 6300 H-1B visas and almost 3000 green cards. If you do the math for every worker that Microsoft laid off they replace that worker with one and a half foreign indentured servants," he said. Vance said the administration's ongoing investigation had led to Microsoft's suspension from the programme. "That's a scandalous system we've allowed in this country for far too long but thanks to the work of this task force and the empowerment of the President of the United States we are going to stop because thanks to an ongoing investigation we suspend the program for Microsoft which means they will no longer able to take those visas and apply for permanent status," he added He also said the Trump administration wanted companies operating in the US to expand while prioritising American workers. "Our message to Microsoft in any other foreign or domestic corporation is simple. We want you to thrive in the United States of America. We want people to invest in the united states of America particularly the American technology sector, we are the biggest boosters of your industry. We want you to be able to grow and employ a lot of people but we want you to employ American workers. You are a great American company but you have to hire great American workers. You cannot lay off American workers and replace them with foreign indentured service," the US VP said. The US Labour secretary further said the department would not accept new applications or process pending permanent labor certification applications involving the companies. "We will not accept any new or process any pending permanent labor certification applications involving these companies," Sonderling said. Sonderling said the companies named had collectively sought millions of foreign workers and received hundreds of thousands of H-1B visa approvals and permanent labor certifications. "Since 2009, just these companies alone have requested almost 3 million foreign workers. They received over 230,000 H1B Visa approvals and over 100,000 permanent labor certifications that's hundred and thousands of jobs that were taken from a American workers," the Labor Secretary said. The announcement comes a day after the US Department of Homeland Security proposed new fees for F-1 nonimmigrant students seeking to participate in Optional Practical Training (OPT), describing the measure as an effort to protect American workers and strengthen the integrity of the immigration system. Under the proposed rule announced on October 7, DHS would establish a USD 70,000 fee per F-1 nonimmigrant student for initial OPT and a USD 30,000 fee for any subsequent OPT. According to DHS, the proposal is aimed at reducing the flow of cheap labour into the United States, combating fraud and abuse, and making it easier for American citizens to compete in the job market. "Optional Practical Training was never meant to be a back door into the American workforce, a subsidy for cheap labor, or a prize for those who game the system," a DHS spokesperson said. "DHS is upskilling OPT to require foreign students to justify their worth to employers. American workers should not have to compete against a program that has been turned into a pipeline for cheap foreign labor." Under existing federal regulations, eligible F-1 students can participate in OPT when the employment is directly related to their major area of study. Students require a recommendation from their designated school official and must apply for employment authorisation with US Citizenship and Immigration Services. Eligible students can receive up to 12 months of OPT at each education level, while those who earn degrees in science, technology, engineering or mathematics fields may qualify for an additional 24-month extension. DHS said the proposed changes followed fraud and abuse identified by the Student and Exchange Visitor Program, including schemes involving problematic worksites and "pay-to-stay" visa arrangements. The proposed fees would be paid by SEVP-certified schools before designated school officials recommend students for OPT in the Student and Exchange Visitor Information System and before students apply for employment authorisation with USCIS. DHS said the proposed fee would apply when schools recommend an F-1 student for any type of OPT and would not be tied to a particular employer. Collected fees would be deposited in the US Treasury. The department will accept public comments on the proposed rule from October 8 through November 9, while the Paperwork Reduction Act section will have a separate 60-day public comment period. (ANI)

item.title: French students keep up protest pressure with some demonstrations hit by violence
item.description: French teenagers blockaded some high schools and marched through cities on Thursday in the latest wave of nationwide protests about conditions in the country's schools, and some of the demonstrations were marred by violent unrest.
item.dc:creator: Manon Cruz, Dominique Vidalon
item.content:encoded: French teenagers blockaded some high schools and marched through cities on Thursday in the latest wave of nationwide protests about conditions in the country's schools, and some of the demonstrations were marred by violent unrest. The Interior Ministry said 71,500 people participated in the day's demonstrations, of which 24,500 took part in the main Paris protest centred around the Bastille square. The Paris protest was mostly peaceful, although there were occasional clashes between small groups of demonstrators and the police during the evening. Elsewhere, arsonists attacked a [USN:FWN45U1T1 TEXT:"Bordeaux"] police station, a school in Saint-Etienne was ransacked and a teacher in Toulouse was hit by a demonstrator, said the Interior Ministry. In Marseille, police said a teacher at Victor Hugo High School [USN:FWN45U1T4 TEXT:"was attacked"] during the latest protests and has filed a criminal complaint over the incident. Protesters clash with French gendarmes, as French high school and university students attend a demonstration, as part of a nationwide day of protests and blockades to demand better school conditions, in Nantes, France, October 8, 2026. REUTERS/Stephane Mahe A water cannon sprays protesters during a demonstration by French high school and university students in Paris as part of a nationwide day of protests and blockades supported by teachers and school parents to demand better school conditions in France, October 8.
